defendant: S&P Data Ohio, LLC (1500 West Third Street, Cleveland, OH 44113)
agreement: "Grant Agreement" between JobsOhio as Grantor and S&P Data Ohio, LLC as Grantee, for up to $150,000.00 in grant funds "on a reimbursement basis." Amended by an "Amendment to Grant Agreement" on or about June 14, 2018 (Exhibit 2). The complaint calls the two together the "Grant Agreement." The agreement itself is headed "JOBSOHIO GRANT AGREEMENT" and recites that "Grantee will use the financial assistance in accordance with JobsOhio's grant guidelines to invest in workforce training associated with Grantee's project at the Project Address."
agreement_date: The complaint pleads "On or about April 8, 2018" (para. 4), and the September 12, 2023 demand letter also says "dated April 8, 2018." The attached agreement itself states "Effective Date: February 6, 2018." Both dates are read directly from the filing; the complaint and the exhibit do not agree. Amendment to Grant Agreement on or about June 14, 2018.
program: Not named as one of JobsOhio's published programs in the complaint. The attached agreement carries "Program No.: SFPN_2017_441860-WF" in its header grid, and its recital describes the use as "invest in workforce training." No program name appears anywhere in the complaint.
amount_sought: $150,000.00, plus interest including prejudgment interest, reasonable attorney fees, costs and expenses. Notably, JobsOhio's own September 12, 2023 demand letter had demanded only $75,000.00 and said that figure was "non-negotiable." The complaint explains the jump: because the company did not pay the $75,000 within 30 days, "JobsOhio therefore seeks damages in the entire amount of the grant funds provided to Defendant, being $150,000.00" (para. 11).
job_commitments: From the first page of the attached Grant Agreement: No. of Jobs to be Created: 180; Total Payroll to be Created: $6,000,000; No. of Jobs to be Retained: 122; Total Payroll to be Retained: $5,197,754; No. of Employees to be Trained: 225; Total Training Investment: $359,307. Effective Date February 6, 2018; Metric Evaluation Date December 31, 2020; Metric Expiration Date December 31, 2022. Project Site 1500 West Third Street, Cleveland, OH 44113 (Cuyahoga County).
shortfall: Per the company's own 2022 Annual Report, as pleaded at para. 9 and repeated in the demand letter: "Defendant only created 136 new jobs at the Project Site, instead of the required 180 new jobs, and the new jobs had an associated payroll of $4,000,000.00, instead of the required payroll of at least $6,000,000.00." The complaint does not state what happened to the retention, training-headcount or training-investment metrics.
repayment_quote:
QUOTED IN THE COMPLAINT (para. 5, Section 5 of the Grant Agreement): "5. Metrics and Maintenance of Operations. Grantor has approved an award of financial assistance to Grantee to induce Grantee to undertake and complete the Project with the goal of attracting and retaining business opportunities for the State of Ohio that create and/or retain a significant number of jobs for Ohioans. Accordingly, achieving Grantee's Metric Commitment obligations at the Project site during the Term are essential terms of this Agreement. *** (a) Metric Commitment. Grantee must attain all Metric Commitments set forth on the first page of this Agreement no later than the Metric Evaluation Date. Once Metric Commitments have been met, Grantee shall maintain such Metric Commitments through the Metric Expiration Date. *** (c) Remedy. If Grantee fails to satisfy its obligations under Section 5(a), Section 6(b), or to maintain substantial operations at the Project site during the Term, Grantee is in default of this Agreement and Grantor may seek the remedies provided to Grantor under section 9 of this Agreement. *** (Emphasis added)."

QUOTED IN THE COMPLAINT (para. 6, Section 6(b)): "(b) Annual Reports. Grantee shall submit to Grantor an annual report in the format required by Grantor (the "Annual Report"). Each Annual Report shall provide information for the applicable reporting period detailing the progress of the Project, and Metric Commitments to date. Annual Reports shall be submitted by Grantee for each calendar year (or part of a year) during the Term of this Agreement, and each Annual Report shall be received by Grantor no later than March 1 following the calendar year covered by such Annual Report. Failure by Grantee to submit any Annual Report shall be a default for which Grantor may terminate this Agreement as set forth in Section 9. (Emphasis added)."

QUOTED IN THE COMPLAINT (para. 7, Sections 9(a) and 9(b) "in pertinent part"): "(a) Breach. Grantee shall be deemed to be in "Breach" of this Agreement if: *** (ii) Grantee fails to comply with the Metric Commitment requirements set forth in Section 5 hereof; (iii) Grantee fails to timely comply with its reporting obligations under Section 6 hereof; (iv) Grantee fails to maintain substantial operations at the Project Address during the Term. *** (b) Effect of Breach; Remedies. In the event of a Breach by Grantor, Grantee may pursue any legal or equitable remedies it may have under this Agreement or applicable law. In the event of a Breach by Grantee, Grantor may terminate this Agreement and may in addition exercise one or more of the following remedies: *** (ii) Demand Repayment of Grant Funds. Grantor may demand repayment of all or a portion of Grant Funds disbursed. Grantee shall repay such Grant Funds within thirty (30) days after written demand by Grantor. (Emphasis added). (iii) Other Legal Remedies. Pursue any other legal or equitable remedies Grantor may have under this Agreement or applicable law."

FROM THE AGREEMENT ITSELF, ATTACHED AS EXHIBIT 1 (Section 9, text the complaint did not block-quote): "9. Default and Remedies. Except to the extent that this Agreement or applicable law requires otherwise, the remedies set forth in this Section are the sole and exclusive remedies available upon a violation, default or Breach of this Agreement." Section 9(a) lists ten Breach triggers, (i) through (x), including "(vii) Grantee admits its inability to pay its debts as such debts become due; (viii) Grantee commences a voluntary bankruptcy; (ix) an involuntary bankruptcy action occurs against Grantee which remains undismissed or unstayed for sixty (60) days; or (x) Grantee has ceased operations at the Project Address for a period greater than ninety (90) consecutive days." Section 9(b)(i) adds "Discontinue Disbursements. If the Grant Funds have not been fully disbursed, Grantor may terminate any and all of Grantor's obligations under this Agreement, including the obligation to make further disbursements of Grant Funds." Section 9(d): "Remedies Cumulative. No remedy provided to Grantor under this agreement or otherwise by law or in equity is exclusive of any other available remedy." Section 9(e): "Grantor's Expenses. Grantee shall reimburse Grantor for all expenses, including, without limitation, reasonable attorneys' fees, in connection with the enforcement of this Agreement."

ALSO FROM THE ATTACHED AGREEMENT, the discretion clauses that do not appear in the complaint's block quotes. Section 5(a) ends: "Notwithstanding the terms of this Agreement, Grantor has the discretion to determine compliance." Section 5(c) ends: "Notwithstanding, Grantor has the discretion to waive non-compliance if, in writing, Grantee submits to Grantor a description of Market Conditions and Other Factors regarding Grantee and its operations at the Project site. Grantor will review and consider such Market Conditions and Other Factors submitted and may waive repayment of all or a portion of the Grant Funds disbursed." Section 5(d) defines them: "As used herein, "Market Conditions and Other Factors" include, without limitation: an overall decline in economic performance, as a whole or in Grantee's relevant sector, during the term of this Agreement; whether the Grantee obtains a written agreement of a purchaser of the facility to assume the job creation and retention obligations set forth in the Agreement; whether a relocation of the operations of the Project is within the State of Ohio and employs an equivalent number of jobs; Grantee's overall presence in the State of Ohio; and any other information Grantor determines in its reasonable judgment to be relevant under the circumstances."

FROM THE DEMAND LETTER, EXHIBIT 3, September 12, 2023, JobsOhio letterhead, signed by Don Grubbs, General Counsel: "In its 2022 Annual Report, however, Grantee reported it had created only 136 new jobs with an associated payroll of $4,000,000. Therefore, pursuant to Section 9(a) of the Agreement, Grantee is in Breach of the Agreement. As a result of this Breach, and pursuant to Section 9(b)(ii) of the Agreement, JobsOhio demands that Grantee repay to JobsOhio the Grant Funds disbursed under the Agreement, in the amount of $75,000. The amount demanded to be repaid takes into account the number of jobs and payroll Grantee created, the total fixed assets invested in the Project, as well as the Market Conditions and Other Factors provided by Grantee to JobsOhio. Please note this amount is non-negotiable."
remedy_named: "Demand Repayment of Grant Funds" (Section 9(b)(ii)), under the heading "Default and Remedies" (Section 9) and "Effect of Breach; Remedies" (Section 9(b)). Section 5(c) is headed "Remedy." The words clawback and liquidated damages do not appear anywhere in this agreement or complaint. Section 5(c) and 5(d) give JobsOhio discretion to "waive repayment of all or a portion of the Grant Funds disbursed" on "Market Conditions and Other Factors."
agreement_is_exhibit: Yes. The full executed Grant Agreement is attached as Exhibit 1 (DocuSign envelope, signed), the Amendment to Grant Agreement as Exhibit 2, and the demand letter as Exhibit 3. This complaint does not withhold the agreement and gives no confidentiality reason. This is the opposite of the practice in the Olive AI complaint (23CV005498), which refused to attach the agreement as confidential/trade secret.
outcome: Default judgment for JobsOhio. No attorney ever appeared for S&P Data Ohio. JobsOhio moved for default judgment on 02/15/2024. On 04/02/2024 Judge Dan Hawkins signed an "ORDER GRANTING PLAINTIFF JOBSOHIO JUDGMENT AGAINST DEFENDANT S&P DATA OHIO, LLC": "ORDERED that JobsOhio is granted judgment against Defendant S&P Data Ohio, LLC in the amount of $150,000.00, plus costs and statutory interest from the date of this Judgment." Case terminated the same day. On 10/15/2025 JobsOhio filed a "NOTICE OF SATISFACTION OF JUDGMENT AND RELEASE OF JUDGMENT LIEN": "Now comes the Plaintiff JobsOhio and hereby gives notice that the judgment herein has been satisfied, and JobsOhio releases any judgment lien."
amount_recovered: Judgment of $150,000.00 recorded as satisfied on 2025-10-15. No filing states the sum actually paid, who paid it, or whether interest and costs were included. The satisfaction notice names no dollar figure.

notes: The most important finding in this case is that the full executed JobsOhio Grant Agreement is in the public record, attached as Exhibit 1. It is a workforce-training grant on a reimbursement basis, Program No. SFPN_2017_441860-WF. Second finding: the gap between the demand and the suit. JobsOhio demanded $75,000, half the award, and called the figure non-negotiable; when the company did not pay within the 30 days Section 9(b)(ii) allows, JobsOhio sued for the whole $150,000 and took judgment for the whole $150,000. Third: the agreement gives JobsOhio sole discretion both to "determine compliance" (5(a)) and to "waive repayment of all or a portion of the Grant Funds disbursed" (5(c)), on factors it alone weighs. Fourth: the complaint and the attached agreement disagree on the agreement's date, April 8, 2018 versus an Effective Date of February 6, 2018. Grant schedule shows $650,000 paid to this recipient across 2018 and 2021; this suit concerns only a $150,000 agreement, so the other payments were under instruments not in this docket. The company's 2022 Annual Report numbers come to the court only through JobsOhio's pleading; the report itself is not in the record. Two judges appear on the case, Dan Hawkins on the judgment and Richard D Brown on the satisfaction, because of mass courtroom transfers on 12/30/2024 and 01/03/2025 shown on the docket.
